title: Cross-Team Release Signal Contracts — Scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This scratchpad captures a lightweight, engineering-friendly approach to defining signal contracts for cross-functional releases (canaries, micro-rollouts, and A/B experiments). Intention is to produce minimal, testable contracts that allow product, SRE, ML infra, and CS to agree on "signals of truth" and automated gating behavior before exposure.

Audience:
- Product owners running feature rollouts
- SRE/oncall responsible for safety gates
- ML infra and serving engineers (runtime, batching, model variants)
- Customer Success/Support for impact triage

High-level constraints we want:
- Signals should be actionable (clear threshold -> action)
- Each signal must map to an instrumented metric and a primary owner
- Signals grouped into: Safety (errors, latency), Cost (per-token spend, throughput), Quality (automated evals, user-facing failure rate), Behavioral (hallucination proxies, content-safety flags)
- Make automated fallback decisions deterministic and auditable

Signal Catalog (starter):
1) Safety/Error rate
   - slug: safety.error_rate_30m
   - definition: rolling 30m user-facing error rate (HTTP 500s and model runtime errors / requests)
   - owner: eng-sre
   - alert threshold (soft): 0.5%
   - abort threshold: 1.5%
   - action: scale down exposure by 50% -> notify oncall -> if persists for 15m, rollback to baseline

2) Tail latency (p99 response time for end-to-end request)
   - slug: latency.p99_e2e_15m
   - owner: serving-runtime
   - soft threshold: 1200ms
   - abort threshold: 2200ms
   - action: divert new traffic to cheaper/compatible model variant or reduce batch size, depending on policy; escalate if fallback unavailable

3) Cost per effective token (estimate)
   - slug: cost.eff_token_1h
   - definition: avg weighted compute cost per token across model variants for the cohort
   - owner: infra-finops
   - soft threshold: +15% vs baseline
   - abort threshold: +40% vs baseline
   - action: auto-switch to quantized / lower-epoch variant for non-high-priority cohorts

4) Quality regression (eval set delta)
   - slug: quality.eval_delta_30m
   - definition: automated eval suite score delta vs pinned baseline; includes n-gram overlap, rag correctness, safety filter pass-rate
   - owner: applied-ml
   - soft threshold: -2 points (relative)
   - abort threshold: -5 points
   - action: pause expansion of cohorts, route to canary reviewers, mark release for rollback if paired with other signals

5) Hallucination proxy (fact-check fail rate)
   - slug: quality.halluc_proxy
   - owner: applied-ml / product
   - threshold: domain-specific; include manual sampling cadence in contract

Instrumentation checklist (minimum):
- Every signal must have: metric name, query (PromQL/SQL), dashboard tile id, alert rule id, and test harness that can synthesize the signal in staging
- Synthetic traffic generator: small script to emulate 1–10% cohort traffic at scale with configurable prompt mixes (edge long-context, short prompts, bursts)
- Schema for logs: request_id, model_variant, batch_size, prompt_len, response_len, token_cost_estimate, eval_flags, safety_flags
- Tagging: every rollout event must tag traffic with rollout_id, cohort_id, and stage (canary/primary/ab-control)

Gating and decision semantics (how to interpret signals together):
- Use a three-tier decision model: Observed -> Investigate -> Act
- Observed: single soft threshold breach (auto-notify, increase sampling, pause expansion)
- Investigate: persistent or multiple concurrent soft breaches within 30m (run diagnostics playbook, attach owner)
- Act (automated): abort threshold hit for any single critical safety signal, or two abort-threshold hits across safety+quality/cost within a 20m window
- Automated actions must be reversible and annotated with metadata (who/what triggered, timestamp, snapshot of metric queries)

Rollback decision tree (quick):
1) Critical safety abort -> immediate rollback to baseline, page SRE & PM, save artifacts
2) Severe quality abort without safety issues but reproducible eval regression -> pause expansion, require gated manual approval to continue (owner: applied-ml + PM)
3) Cost abort -> switch to cheaper variant or rate-limit cohorts; if persistent >2 hours escalate to infra-finops for budget decision

Exposure choreography (ops steps for rolling out new LLM-backed route):
- Preflight (pre-roll): define signal contract, run synthetic traffic test, create dashboard snapshot, register rollout_id in release registry
- Launch step 0: 1% micro-cohort for 10m, monitor core signals, manual sanity check of 20 samples by reviewers
- Launch step 1: 5% for 30m if all soft checks clean; enable expanded automated evals
- Launch step 2: 20% for 1h with tightened sampling of user sessions and CS monitoring windows
- Promote to global if no aborts and metric deltas within thresholds for 24h

Comms and incident playback obligations: (keep short)
- Owner who triggered action must post a timestamped note in #rollouts with: rollout_id, metric snapshots, action taken, link to dashboard and traces
- Within 4 business hours an initial incident blameless note must be created in Confluence; 72h postmortem if rollback occurred

Open questions / tradeoffs we need resolve:
- How to standardize "quality" signals across very different consumer features (search vs. composer vs. assistant)? Proposed: a feature-level min-suite + global safety suite
- How aggressive should automated cost mitigations be for enterprise customers with reserved capacity? Suggest policy: enterprise-tier explicit opt-out for auto-cost switches; require billing owner approval
- Sampling strategy for manual review: dynamic sampling vs fixed quota — leaning dynamic with priority weighting for high-impact cohorts

Immediate next steps (this doc is a scratchpad):
- Aisha: convert this to a compact signal-contract template (1 pager) and push to confluence draft
- Marco: prototype synthetic traffic harness and add to ci/staging playbook (owner: rollout-tests)
- Lena: map current dashboards to the starter signal catalog and surface missing instrumentation gaps

Quick links / artifacts:
- Jira: PROD-1123 (release registry prototype), PROD-1199 (signal exporter work)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-configs#78

Notes to self: keep contracts small and testable. The goal is not to capture every metric but to pick the smallest set that reliably correlates with user harm or heavy cost drift.
